case_title.quote: CHOTKAU v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH

number_of_accused.quote: the sole accused has come up with the above appeals

accused_gender.quote: the appellant herein took his niece

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused is given anywhere in the judgment.

accused_occupation.correct_value: Labourer (brothers engaged as labourers; occupation of accused not directly stated)
accused_occupation.quote: All the three of them are engaged in the occupation of labourers.
accused_occupation.reason: PW-2 said accused's brothers are labourers; accused's own occupation is not expressly stated.

accused_socioeconomic_status.correct_value: Poor; could not afford a lawyer
accused_socioeconomic_status.quote: the appellant is so poor that he could not afford to engage a lawyer even in the Sessions Court
accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Judgment states the appellant is poor.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Fellow villager/neighbour; no kinship stated (victim was niece of the informant)
accused_victim_relationship.quote: the appellant herein took his niece aged about 6 years
accused_victim_relationship.reason: 'His' refers to the complainant Kishun Bahadur, not the accused; no relation to the accused is stated.

offence_category.quote: Rape and murder – Conviction for, and death sentence
offence_category.reason: Charged with both rape and murder; only Murder listed.

statutory_provisions.quote: Sections 302 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code

evidence_type.quote: the prosecution of the appellant is based on circumstantial evidence

confession.reason: No confession; accused denied the charges.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Victim was a six-year-old girl raped and murdered; courts below found it rarest of rare
aggravating_circumstances.quote: one of the rarest of rare cases where a six year old girl had been raped and murdered
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Lower courts relied on aggravating factors, so 'Not stated' is inaccurate.

mitigating_circumstances.correct_value: Accused was poor and could not afford a lawyer
mitigating_circumstances.quote: the appellant is so poor that he could not afford to engage a lawyer
mitigating_circumstances.reason: The judgment mentions the appellant's poverty.

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted the appellant for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 376 of the IPC and awarded death penalty

high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court did decide; it confirmed the conviction and sentence.

final_outcome.quote: the appeals are allowed and the conviction and penalty are set aside

offence_finally_established.quote: we are not convinced that the guilt of the appellant stood established beyond reasonable doubt

neutral_facts.correct_value: Should note the girl was the niece of the informant, not the accused; otherwise consistent and non-outcome-revealing
neutral_facts.quote: took his niece aged about 6 years under the pretext of showing dance and song performances
neutral_facts.reason: Largely accurate and outcome-neutral; the date and event details are fine, but PW roles are slightly simplified.

offence_severity.correct_value: Not stated (courts below imposed death penalty)
offence_severity.reason: The 7-10 years range appears nowhere in the judgment.

attempt_completion.reason: Offence alleged completed, but the SC did not find it established.

physical_harm.quote: the dead body of the girl was found in the sugarcane field

number_of_offences.correct_value: Charged with 2 offences, 0 upheld by SC (convictions set aside)
number_of_offences.quote: the conviction and penalty are set aside

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: SC accepted no key prosecution evidence; it rejected the last-seen evidence of PWs 1-3 as untrustworthy
key_evidence_accepted.quote: These contradictions make the evidence of PWs 1 to 3 completely untrustworthy.
key_evidence_accepted.reason: SC did not accept the circumstantial evidence or last seen theory.

witness_credibility.quote: These contradictions make the evidence of PWs 1 to 3 completely untrustworthy.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Accused allegedly absconded and was seen leaving the sugarcane field
post_offence_conduct.quote: the dead body was found and the appellant was absconding
post_offence_conduct.reason: Prosecution case included absconding and leaving the field; the judgment does state this.

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence 08.03.2012; HC judgment 18.04.2016; SC 28.09.2022; trial judgment date not stated
trial_duration.quote: From the Judgment and Order dated 18.04.2016 of the High Court
trial_duration.reason: 18.04.2016 is the High Court's date, not the trial court's.

legal_representation.quote: S. Nagamuthu, Sr. Adv., Ms. Shivani Misra...

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR registered, investigation, charge sheet filed, trial completed; investigation found deficient
investigation_status.quote: By not conducting the investigation properly
investigation_status.reason: Accurate but omits the court's criticism of the investigation.

procedural_irregularity.quote: delay of 5 days in transmitting the FIR to the jurisdictional court, especially in the facts and circumstances of this case was fatal

appeal_history.quote: the High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence

prosecution_argument.correct_value: The State argued PWs 1-3 had no reason to implicate the appellant, FIR delay did not prejudice, s.313 defect needs prejudice, and forensic evidence is not always mandatory
prosecution_argument.quote: the delay in forwarding the FIR to the court did not vitiate the trial
prosecution_argument.reason: Omits the State's arguments on FIR delay, s.313 and forensic evidence.

defence_argument.correct_value: Also argued insufficient last seen evidence, non-examination of material witnesses, s.313 non-compliance, and false implication by Zalim Khan
defence_argument.quote: the mandatory requirement of Section 313 of the Code was not fulfilled
defence_argument.reason: Incomplete; omits several defence arguments including false implication.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Panchsheel principles for circumstantial evidence, plus the effect of FIR delay and failure to conduct medical examination when ocular evidence is untrustworthy
legal_principle_applied.quote: there must be a chain of evidence so complete as not to leave any reasonable ground
legal_principle_applied.reason: Correct but omits the decisive grounds.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Matches the list of cases relied on.

sentencing_rationale.quote: it is one of the rarest of rare cases
sentencing_rationale.reason: Lower courts' rationale and SC reversal accurately described.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: SC acquitted; no sentencing mitigating factors considered.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: SC identified none, since it acquitted.

other_sentence_order.quote: The appellant shall be released forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case.
